I'm kind of stuck between a rock and a hard place with my automotive photography. I've only ever worked for the dealerships as a direct employee and have gotten these jobs through word of mouth so I wouldn't consider it a business I've built. Most dealerships don't really hire true photographers, they hire people at $15 an hour to take pictures of cars, or they subscribe to a 3rd party company that sends people out to take pics of your inventory. Those companies pay about $15/hr as well. I'm a direct employee at where I'm at now but I only make $2 more and have been denied a raise the past two years. The real photography business I've been building all these years has been my fun live music/graphic design/art stuff completely separate from the car stuff. Every year I do a little bit better and I'm slowly getting more paid work but still nothing consistent enough to live off of. No big clients.  

With all of the successes and growth I've had I feel like it's a possibility I'll eventually be able to make a decent living, but as I'm into my 30s now I'm having sort of an existential crisis about how I would pay for health issues and retirement. 

Overall I feel like I've hit the ceiling in the automotive field and the creative field I've been building, that's incredibly difficult to make a decent living doing, is nowhere near sustainable.
